recipes.title: Peruvian Lime‑Chili Roast Chicken with Garlic Rice

recipe.title: Peruvian Lime‑Chili Roast Chicken with Garlic Rice
recipe.description: Tender chicken breasts marinated in lime juice and yellow chili paste, roasted until juicy, served over fragrant garlic rice. A light, aromatic dinner inspired by Perú’s classic pollo a la brasa.
instructions: Mix the yellow chili paste, lime juice, 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch black pepper in a bowl.
Slice the red onion thinly; add to the marinade and stir.
Add the 2 chicken breasts, coat well, and let marinate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
While the chicken marinates, rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat, add the minced garlic and sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the rice, stir 2 minutes to toast lightly, then add 400 ml water, a pinch of salt and bring to a boil.
Reduce to low heat, cover and simmer 15 minutes until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Pre‑heat the oven to 200 °C. Place the marinated chicken on a baking sheet and roast 20 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 74 °C and the juices run clear.
Let the chicken rest 5 minutes, then slice diagonally.
Serve the sliced chicken over the garlic rice, garnish with extra lime wedges if desired.
tips: For extra crispness, broil the chicken for the last 2 minutes.
If you prefer a milder flavor, reduce the chili paste to 1 tbsp.
recipe.image_prompt: Professional food photography, golden‑brown Peruvian roast chicken slices over fluffy garlic rice, lime wedges and red onion rings, rustic wooden plate, natural light

issues: La recette mentionne de l'ail dans les ingrédients, mais il n'est pas dans le garde-manger fourni (bien que toléré selon les règles, cela reste une entorse à la gestion des stocks).
strengths: Les repères de cuisson sont excellents, notamment la température interne de 74°C pour la volaille.
L'ordre des étapes est parfaitement logique, permettant une gestion efficace du temps pendant la cuisson du riz.

recipes.title: Brazilian Corn & Rice Soup (Caldo de Milho)

recipe.title: Brazilian Corn & Rice Soup (Caldo de Milho)
recipe.description: A comforting, light soup made with sweet corn kernels, rice, and a hint of lime. Perfect for an easy dinner that highlights Brazil’s love of corn.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil over medium heat.
Add the 3 corn cobs, cover and boil 10 minutes until the kernels are tender.
Remove the cobs, let cool, then cut the kernels off the cob with a sharp knife; set kernels aside.
In the same pot, heat olive oil over medium heat, add the finely diced red onion and sauté 4 minutes until translucent.
Stir in the yellow chili paste and cook 1 minute, releasing its aroma.
Add the rice and toast 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in 800 ml fresh water, bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat and simmer 15 minutes, or until the rice is soft.
Add the corn kernels, lime zest, and a pinch of salt and pepper; cook 5 minutes more until the soup is heated through.
Check seasoning and adjust if needed.
Ladle the soup into bowls and serve hot.
tips: For a richer broth, replace part of the water with low‑salt chicken stock (if available).
Blend half of the soup for a creamier texture, then stir back in the remaining whole kernels.
recipe.image_prompt: Warm bowl of Brazilian corn and rice soup, creamy broth with bright yellow corn kernels, a sprinkle of lime zest, rustic ceramic bowl, steam rising, natural light

issues: L'utilisation de l'eau comme base unique pour le bouillon rend la soupe très fade par rapport à un vrai 'caldo' brésilien qui nécessite généralement un fond de volaille ou de lait.
strengths: La technique de récupération des grains de maïs après ébullition est bien expliquée et sécurisée.
Le respect des quantités dans chaque étape est exemplaire.

recipes.title: Argentinian Grilled Corn & Chicken with Chimichurri‑Style Lime Potatoes

recipe.title: Argentinian Grilled Corn & Chicken with Chimichurri‑Style Lime Potatoes
recipe.description: Grilled corn cobs and chicken breasts brushed with a tangy lime‑chili sauce, served alongside crispy potatoes tossed in a chimichurri‑inspired lime dressing. A festive, light dinner with distinct Argentine flavors.
instructions: Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium‑high heat and preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Peel the potatoes, cut them into 2‑cm cubes, and place in a bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp lime juice (squeezed from the limes), chopped parsley, a pinch of salt and a pinch of black pepper.
Toss the potato cubes with the lime‑parsley mixture; set aside.
Slice the red onion into thick rings.
Mix the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp yellow chili paste and 1 tbsp lime juice; brush this onto both sides of the chicken breasts.
Place the chicken on the grill and cook for 6‑7 minutes per side, or until the internal temperature reaches 74 °C and the juices run clear. Remove and let rest for 5 minutes.
While the chicken cooks, brush the corn cobs with a little olive oil and grill for 8‑10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, until the kernels are lightly charred.

Spread the seasoned potato cubes on a baking sheet in a single layer, drizzle any leftover dressing over them, and bake for 20 minutes, turning halfway, until the potatoes are golden, crisp, and tender when pierced with a fork.
Slice the rested chicken, arrange on a plate with the grilled corn, potato wedges, and raw onion rings.
Finish with a drizzle of any remaining lime‑parsley oil and a final pinch of salt.
tips: For extra smoky flavor, add a few drops of liquid smoke to the potato dressing.
If you prefer a spicier kick, increase the chili paste to 1½ tbsp.
recipe.image_prompt: Vibrant Argentine dinner plate with grilled chicken slices, charred corn on the cob, golden crisp potatoes tossed in lime‑parsley dressing, red onion rings, rustic wooden board, outdoor lighting

issues: L'étape 9 demande de cuire les pommes de terre au four alors que le grill est déjà allumé, ce qui est une gestion énergétique peu optimale.
Le persil n'est pas dans le garde-manger initial, bien qu'il soit listé comme ingrédient.
strengths: La précision des temps de cuisson pour le grill et le four est très rigoureuse.
La gestion de la sécurité alimentaire avec le repos de la viande est parfaitement respectée.
